name: Google Assistant
description: Google's voice assistant on phones, speakers and cars for about a decade.
cause: Pivoted away — Google retired it and replaced it with Gemini everywhere.

name: Notion Mail
description: Notion's AI email app that sorted your inbox and drafted replies for you.
cause: Shutdown — Notion closed it after only 17 months.

name: Relay.app
description: Automation tool that connected your apps and ran tasks with AI help.
cause: Shutdown — the founder and part of the team joined Google Chrome and the service ended.

name: Beatoven.ai
description: AI music maker that created royalty-free background tracks for videos and podcasts.
cause: Pivoted away — discontinued its consumer music app in September 2026; the core team joined Rusk Media and the company kept its tech for business licensing.

name: Reve
description: AI image maker praised for sharp text inside images and strong prompt following.
cause: Pivoted away — after OpenAI invested and hired some of its researchers, Reve stopped new sign-ups and ended image generation on September 27, 2026, moving on to other AI work.

name: ChatGPT Atlas
description: OpenAI's AI web browser with ChatGPT built into every tab.
cause: Shutdown — OpenAI discontinued it less than a year after launch.

name: Pixel Studio
description: Google's phone app for making and editing AI images from text.
cause: Shutdown — Google disabled the app and pointed users to Gemini instead.

name: Qlip
description: AI clip maker that cut long videos and webinars into short, captioned clips for social media.
cause: Acquired and killed — Livestorm bought Qlip in 2026 and folded its clipping tech into Livestorm AI Studio; the standalone product was wound down.

name: Huxe
description: Made short personalized audio briefings and podcasts based on your interests.
cause: Shutdown — built by ex-NotebookLM developers; closed about a year after raising $4.6M.

name: Dora AI
description: Built animated 3D websites from a single text prompt, no code needed.
cause: Shutdown — closed the same day as its sister product Gambo; the site went fully offline with no successor.

name: LOVO
description: AI voice studio (Genny) for voiceovers, voice cloning and text-to-speech.
cause: Shutdown — filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on May 27, 2026, in the middle of a voice-actor lawsuit over unauthorized voice clones; paying users had been locked out since April.

name: Sora
description: OpenAI's video maker that turned text prompts into short, realistic clips.
cause: Shutdown — it reportedly cost about $1M a day to run, users fell under 500k, and Disney's $1B deal died with it; the API followed in September 2026.

name: Yupp
description: Playground where you chatted with two AI models side by side and voted for the better answer.
cause: Shutdown — closed with 1.3M users despite a $33M seed round.

name: Clockwise
description: AI calendar assistant that moved your meetings around to protect blocks of focus time.
cause: Shutdown — the AI calendar assistant announced its closure and switched off on March 27, 2026.

name: Kreateable
description: AI design platform for logos, ads and social media graphics.
cause: Shutdown — the site, dashboard and white-label pages all went offline in February 2026 with no announcement.

name: Bento
description: Link-in-bio pages built as a pretty grid of blocks for links, photos and videos.
cause: Acquired and killed — Linktree bought Bento in 2023, kept it running for over two years, then closed it on February 13, 2026 and deleted user pages.

name: Phind
description: AI answer engine for developers that searched the web and explained code.
cause: Shutdown — closed abruptly about a month after raising $10M; user data was deleted two weeks later.

name: Unbounce Smart Copy
description: AI copywriter that wrote ads, emails and landing-page text in your brand voice.
cause: Shutdown — Unbounce discontinued the standalone AI copywriter (born as Snazzy AI) on January 28, 2026 and folded its features into the main landing-page builder.

name: PlayHT
description: Turned text into realistic AI voices and cloned voices for videos, podcasts and apps.
cause: Acquired and killed — Meta hired the whole PlayAI team in July 2025; the API died within weeks and all user voice clones were deleted at the final shutdown.

name: Limitless (Rewind)
description: AI memory app that recorded your meetings and screen so you could search everything later.
cause: Acquired and killed — Meta bought Limitless, stopped Pendant sales and shut the service about two weeks later.

name: Supermaven
description: Very fast AI code autocomplete tool loved by developers.
cause: Acquired and killed — Cursor hired the team and sunset the standalone product.

name: Dot
description: A personal AI companion app that remembered your life and chatted like a friend.
cause: Shutdown — its maker, New Computer, closed the app and told users to export their data first.

name: Humanloop
description: Platform that helped developers test and improve their AI chatbot prompts.
cause: Acquired and killed — Anthropic hired the team and shut the platform down weeks later.

name: Height
description: Project and task app with AI that took routine team busywork off your plate.
cause: Shutdown — the team announced the closure in March 2025 and switched the app off for good on September 24, 2025.

name: Fakespot
description: Used AI to spot fake product reviews on Amazon and other stores.
cause: Shutdown — Mozilla closed it, along with its Firefox Review Checker, to focus on other projects.

name: Cody (Sourcegraph)
description: AI coding assistant that understood your whole codebase.
cause: Pivoted away — Sourcegraph killed the free and personal Pro plans to sell to big companies only.

name: Linkpop
description: Shopify's free link-in-bio page with shoppable product links and built-in checkout.
cause: Shutdown — Shopify retired its free link-in-bio tool on July 7, 2025 with no reason given, pointing sellers to third-party apps instead.

name: Galileo AI
description: Turned a text prompt into a designed app or website interface.
cause: Acquired and killed — Google bought it in May 2025 and folded it into its free Stitch tool.

name: Woebot
description: Therapy-style chatbot that used CBT exercises to help with mood and stress; used by about 1.5M people.
cause: Pivoted away — the consumer app closed because FDA approval was too costly and slow; the company went enterprise-only.

name: Papercup
description: AI dubbing that translated videos into other languages with synthetic voices, used by Sky News and Bloomberg.
cause: Acquired and killed — RWS bought Papercup's AI dubbing technology in June 2025 after much of the team had left, and the standalone company ended.

name: Replica Studios
description: AI voice actors for games and animation, hired from a marketplace of licensed real voices.
cause: Shutdown — ceased operations on June 30, 2025 after it could not raise more funding or reach profitability.

name: Builder.ai
description: Platform that promised apps built by AI 'like ordering pizza'; raised over $450M, backed by Microsoft.
cause: Shutdown — collapsed into insolvency after reports it had inflated its sales numbers.

name: Hour One
description: AI avatar videos — type a script and a virtual presenter reads it on camera.
cause: Acquired and killed — Wix bought Hour One in May 2025 for its tech and team, and the standalone avatar-video product was discontinued.

name: Tome
description: Turned a short prompt into a full slide deck with text and images.
cause: Pivoted away — 20M+ signups but too few paying teams; the team shut it down to build Lightfield, an AI CRM.

name: Humane AI Pin
description: A wearable AI pin with no screen that answered questions by voice and laser projection.
cause: Acquired and killed — HP bought its assets for $116M and the pins stopped working days later.

name: Flowrite
description: AI writing tool that turned a few rough words into ready-to-send emails.
cause: Acquired and killed — Maestro Labs bought Flowrite's email-writing business in January 2025 and folded it into MailMaestro; the standalone app was retired.

name: Figgs AI
description: Free app for creating and roleplaying with AI characters; passed 1M users.
cause: Shutdown — the developers closed it because running the free service cost too much.

name: Moxie
description: A $799 tabletop robot friend for kids, powered by AI conversation.
cause: Shutdown — maker Embodied ran out of money; the robots stopped working and owners got no refunds. The IP was later bought and open-sourced.

name: Forward Health
description: AI health kiosks (CarePods) and app-based clinics that tried to automate the doctor's office.
cause: Shutdown — shut all its clinics and CarePods in November 2024 after the self-service kiosk economics failed to work.

name: OctoAI
description: Cloud service that let companies run open AI models without managing their own servers.
cause: Acquired and killed — NVIDIA bought OctoAI in September 2024 and terminated its hosted model-running service on October 31, 2024.

name: Copilot GPT Builder
description: Let paying Copilot users build their own custom chatbots, like ChatGPT's GPTs.
cause: Shutdown — Microsoft deleted the tool and every GPT users had made, about six months after launch.

name: Xembly
description: AI assistant that took meeting notes and scheduled meetings for you.
cause: Shutdown — the company closed the product in mid-2024.

name: Airgram
description: AI meeting assistant that joined your calls, recorded them and wrote the notes for you.
cause: Pivoted away — the company folded Airgram into its sister app Notta in March 2024 and shut the Airgram product down.

name: Rephrase.ai
description: Made marketing videos with AI avatars that spoke your script.
cause: Acquired and killed — Adobe bought it in late 2023 and folded the tech into Firefly; the standalone product was sunset.

name: Artifact
description: AI news app from Instagram's founders that learned what you liked to read.
cause: Shutdown — the founders closed it after about a year, saying the market was too small; Yahoo later bought the tech.

name: Coqui
description: Open-source text-to-speech that could clone a voice from a few seconds of audio.
cause: Shutdown — the startup wound down at the start of 2024; its open-source models still live on GitHub.

name: MarketMuse
description: AI content planner that told writers which topics and words a page needed to rank on Google.
cause: Acquired and killed — Siteimprove bought it and rolled the tech into its own platform.

name: Koji
description: Link-in-bio pages with mini apps — tip jars, games, polls and storefronts on one page.
cause: Acquired and killed — Linktree bought Koji from GoMeta in December 2023 and shut it down on January 31, 2024, weeks after the deal.

name: Olive
description: AI automation for hospital paperwork and billing; once valued at $4B.
cause: Shutdown — the company wound down and sold its pieces to other health-tech firms.

name: Babylon Health
description: Health app with an AI symptom checker and video doctor visits, once valued at $4.2B.
cause: Shutdown — filed for bankruptcy in August 2023 after its rescue deal collapsed; the US arm was liquidated and the UK business sold to eMed.

name: AI Text Classifier
description: OpenAI's own free tool that tried to detect if a piece of text was written by AI.
cause: Shutdown — OpenAI quietly removed it because its accuracy was too low.

name: Neeva
description: Ad-free, private search engine built by ex-Google leaders.
cause: Acquired and killed — Snowflake bought it for $185M and closed the consumer search engine weeks later.

name: Cortana
description: Microsoft's voice assistant built into Windows.
cause: Pivoted away — Microsoft removed the standalone app and replaced it with Copilot.

name: Mindstrong
description: Mental-health platform that used phone data (digital biomarkers) plus app-based therapy and psychiatry.
cause: Shutdown — wound down in early 2023 and ended patient services on March 10, 2023; its tech assets were then sold to SonderMind.

name: Kite
description: AI code completion that finished your lines of Python and JavaScript as you typed, years before Copilot.
cause: Shutdown — founder Adam Smith closed Kite in November 2022, saying the tech was 10+ years too early and developers would not pay; the code was open-sourced.
